# dsh-train-dashboard

A training dashboard for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH). It adds a **Training
dashboard** tab to the rig

ht pane, beside Files, Terminal and Document, and
charts a JSON snapshot of a training run: a KPI he

ader, one series at a time on
its own axis, the joints that make the series incomparable marked on t

he chart
with the reason for each, and the model's own growth drawn against the reading it
buys.

The plugin does **not** parse your logs. It runs a command of your own, that
command writes the snap

shot JSON described below, and the tab reads it. So the
plugin works with any training setup whose n

umbers you can get into that shape,
and it never competes with your own parser for the truth about a

s you can get into that shape,
and it never competes with your own parser for the truth about a run.

- no build step, no runtime dependencies, plain JavaScript in two files
- no process at all unless a

tab is open and the snapshot is older than
`refreshSeconds`
- never writes anything itself: the sna

pshot is written by your command, and it
is the only file the plugin causes to be written
- the age

of the numbers is always on screen, so a stale chart can never be
mistaken for a live one
- every wo

rd a break marker shows is your snapshot's own: the tab chooses where
a marker sits and how it reads
, never what it says
Package version **0.4.0** — snapshot contract version **1**.
### What changed in 0.4.0

Two features were **removed** and one defect that had been hiding behind them was
fixed. The snapsho

t contract number stays at **1**: every change is additive or
ignored — a snapshot that carries a ke

y this version no longer reads is still
served, and still drawn as far as it can be.

- **No more predictions.** The dashed *frontier* line, its register block, its
switch and the `front

ier` key are gone. A producer's phase length is not
knowable in advance — a phase ends when its read

goes flat, not at a fixed leg
count — so the projection was wrong in its premise, not merely imprec

ise. A
snapshot that still serves `frontier` is served and the key is ignored.
- **No more NO KIND m

arker.** The legacy single-break key `break_leg` — one
constant naming a joint of an arc the snapsho

t no longer charts, carrying no
kind — is no longer folded in, and `/state` no longer republishes it

as
`breakLeg`. A marker whose whole content is that it claims nothing, drawn on a
run that never tr

ained that leg, is not a joint a reader can use.
- **A growth now has a colour and a shape in the ke

y.** The `growth` kind was
added to the chart's shape and ink tables and to no rule in the styleshee

t, so
its register swatch fell back to the sheet's grey and its key drew no shape at
all — a mark on

the chart the register could not decode.
- **The KPI header reads the current bpb tags.** The produ

cer renamed
`train/bpb_sealed` and `train/bpb_legval` to `train/bpb` and
`train/heldout_bpb` on 11 O

ctober 2026, and this tab's headline list was not
moved with them: the headline resolved to nothing

and the first two KPI tiles
read `—` beside four that filled normally. Both spellings are recognised

now,
current first, so an old snapshot on disk still charts.
## What you get
| region | content |

| header | the run's name, the snapshot's age with a fresh/stale badge, a Refresh button |
| KPI row
| latest step, the held-out reading, step wall time, throughput, memory peak, evaluation accuracy,

the seed model's size |
| chips | the eight metrics this tab leads with, and nothing else: `bpb`, `p

pl`, `wall_seconds`, `units/s`, `gnorm`, `read layers`, `VRAM peak`, `vocab_size` |
| chart | ONE se
ries at a time on its own axis, with every break marker drawn on it, over a timeline you can select
— plus the seed model's size as a second dashed line against the axis on the right, the chain a roll
back threw away ghosted beside the live one on a shared origin, and a floating current value for eac

h line |
| register | under the chart: a switch per break category, then one status line per marker
— its kind's shape and colour, its word, its leg and what changed — with the reason, the meaning and

the evidence behind a per-row `why` disclosure |
| footer | the snapshot path being read |

**One series at a time is deliberate.** Series carry different units — bits per
byte, seconds, GiB,

accuracy, counts — and drawing them on one axis would invite
exactly the comparison the axis cannot

support. There is exactly one exception,
and it is the next section.

**The seed model's size is that one exception**, drawn on the same frame against
an axis of its own

on the right — the growth ladder is the point of a run that
adds capacity as it trains, so how big t

he model has become belongs on screen at
the same time as the reading it buys. See
The seed model's

size for what the number is and — more
importantly — what it deliberately is not.

**The chips are the eight metrics the reader asked for, and nothing else.** A
snapshot of this run c

arries sixty series, and an earlier version offered a chip
for a good many of them: the header becam

e a wall of controls, and the one at the
front was a truncated duplicate of the one behind it. The h

eader now offers the
eight above, in that order. **A series outside those eight is not offered as a

eight above, in that order. **A series outside those eight is not offered as a

## What it costs

- **No tab open, no cost.** Nothing is polled and nothing is spawned.
- **Tab open, fresh snapshot.*

* One small JSON read every 5 seconds, and no
process at all.
- **Tab open, stale snapshot.** The sa

me poll, plus your command once per
`refreshSeconds`, single-flight. The only cost the plugin itself

adds is
process start plus one file read; the rest is whatever your producer does, so
make it cheap
or raise `refreshSeconds`.
### Why there is no chart library here

Zero runtime dependencies, no build step, plain JavaScript, and the chart is
hand-written SVG. This
is not minimalism for its own sake:

- the DSH client forbids importing Harness Client packages
